params.q: What is the standard deduction for salaried employees under the new tax regime in India?

search_parameters.q: What is the standard deduction for salaried employees under the new tax regime in India?

response.markdown:
Under the new tax regime, salaried employees in India can claim a **standard deduction of ₹75,000** per year (applicable from FY 2024-25, AY 2025-26, and unchanged for FY 2026-27). [0] [1] [2] This is a flat deduction from gross salary — no proof or documentation is required — and is available to all salaried individuals and pensioners, regardless of their actual expenses. [1] [3] [4]

| Tax Regime | Standard Deduction |
|---|---|
| **New Tax Regime** | **₹75,000** |
| Old Tax Regime | ₹50,000 |

A few quick notes:
- The deduction is applied **once per year**, even if you worked for multiple employers — you cannot claim it separately for each job. [5] [3] [1]
- It is available only against income from the **salary/pension head**, not against other income sources. [3]
- Combined with the ₹4 lakh basic exemption limit and the Section 156 rebate (up to ₹12 lakh of taxable income), salaried individuals earning up to **₹12.75 lakh** effectively pay zero income tax under the new regime for FY 2026-27. [2]
